high.title: 490 Regional Governments Struggle to Pay Employee Salaries, Central Government May Inject Funds
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa revealed that approximately 490 regional governments are facing difficulties paying employee salaries, including contract workers (PPPK), following cuts to regional transfer funds (TKD). The central government is considering injecting additional funds to cover the shortfall, pending presidential directive. This signals significant fiscal stress at the sub-national level and raises concerns about the sustainability of the current regional transfer framework.

high.title: Danantara Joins KSSK Financial Stability Committee Meetings But Has No Policy-Making Authority
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa clarified that Danantara's participation in Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK) meetings is limited to an advisory role, with no voting rights on policy decisions. He confirmed this arrangement is legally permissible under existing law without requiring amendments to the Financial Sector Development and Strengthening Law (UU P2SK). Investors should monitor the growing involvement of the sovereign wealth fund Danantara in financial stability discussions, as it may signal broader policy coordination implications.

high.title: IHSG Closes at Level 6,130, Down 0.89%
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed in the red at 6,130, falling 55 points or 0.89% on Tuesday, July 28, 2026. The index opened already in negative territory at 6,175 and reached an intraday low of 6,130. Total transaction value reached Rp 10.85 trillion, involving 25.43 billion shares traded in 1.67 million transactions.

high.title: Presidential Palace Guarantees BI Governor's Resignation Will Not Disrupt Economy
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo has resigned and is temporarily replaced by Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti, as announced by the Minister of State Secretariat Prasetyo Hadi on Monday, July 27. The government has guaranteed that the transition process will be transparent and will not disrupt monetary policy or national economic stability. This is a significant development for investors as central bank leadership changes can impact monetary policy direction and market confidence.

high.title: Bank Mandiri Posts Rp 30.4 Trillion Net Profit in H1-2026, Up 24.4%
high.summary: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) recorded a net profit of Rp 30.4 trillion through June 2026, representing a strong 24.4% year-on-year growth. The performance was driven by robust business expansion with third-party funds growing 17.1%, loan assets growing 19.9%, and net interest income (NII) growing 8%. Asset quality remained solid with an NPL ratio of 0.98% and cost of credit stable at 0.52%, making this a highly positive result for BMRI shareholders.

high.title: BCA Posts Rp 29.5 Trillion Net Profit, Loans Surpass Rp 1,000 Trillion for First Time
high.summary: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) reported a net profit of Rp 29.5 trillion for the first half of 2026, supported by loan growth of 8% year-on-year that for the first time surpassed the Rp 1,000 trillion milestone, reaching Rp 1,036 trillion. CASA funding grew 10.2% year-on-year to Rp 1,082 trillion, underpinning the bank's solid funding base. This milestone performance is a key indicator of Indonesia's banking sector health and is significant for BBCA investors.

high.title: IDX Asks Investors Not to Panic After Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo Resigns
high.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) is urging investors to remain calm following the sudden resignation of Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo on Monday, July 28. IDX Director of Trading Irvan Susandy acknowledged 2026 has been an exceptionally tough year for Indonesia, citing headwinds from Middle East conflicts, MSCI index review warnings, and Moody's signals. The resignation of the central bank governor is a major market-moving event that could trigger significant volatility in the Rupiah and capital markets.

high.title: Danantara Joins Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK) Alongside BI and OJK by Presidential Order
high.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has ordered state investment vehicle Danantara to participate in every meeting of the Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK), which previously comprised the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, OJK, and LPS. This structural change, announced by Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani, effectively creates a 'KSSK Plus' and gives Danantara a formal role in national financial stability decision-making. This is a significant institutional development that may affect how systemic financial risks and large investment decisions are coordinated in Indonesia.

high.title: Airlangga Still Optimistic Indonesia's Q2 2026 Economy Will Grow Above 5%
high.summary: Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto expressed confidence that Indonesia's economic growth in Q2 2026 will remain above 5%, driven by government incentive packages and strong investment realization. He also projected continued growth in Q3 and Q4, supported by accelerated government spending and investment. This outlook is significant for investors assessing Indonesia's macroeconomic stability amid global uncertainties.

high.title: Danantara Joins KSSK Financial Stability Committee Alongside BI and OJK
high.summary: By order of President Prabowo, state investment vehicle Danantara (BPI) has been officially included in the Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK), which previously consisted only of the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, OJK, and LPS. This structural change expands Danantara's role in systemic financial decision-making, marking a significant shift in Indonesia's financial governance architecture. Investors should monitor how this integration affects policy coordination and the management of state-owned assets.

high.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Further, Down Rp 12,000/gram to Rp 2,601,000
high.summary: Antam 24-karat gold price continued its downward trend, dropping another Rp 12,000 per gram to Rp 2,601,000 — the lowest level in the past month. The buyback price also fell by Rp 15,000 to Rp 2,346,000 per gram, reflecting continued selling pressure in the precious metals market. Over the past month, prices have ranged between Rp 2,601,000 and Rp 2,670,000, signaling a notable correction relevant to commodity and gold investors.

high.title: Foreign Capital Outflow from Indonesian Capital Market Reaches IDR 80.97 Trillion in 2026
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) has faced sustained net foreign selling pressure of IDR 80.97 trillion year-to-date through July 29, 2026. OJK attributes the outflows to global geopolitical risks, global interest rate policy direction, and investor preference shifts toward emerging market assets. The regulator emphasized that foreign fund movements reflect global dynamics rather than Indonesia's domestic market fundamentals.

high.title: GoTo Posts Net Profit Again in Q2, Continuing Positive Performance Streak
high.summary: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) reported a net profit attributable to parent entity owners of IDR 607.5 billion in H1-2026, reversing a loss of IDR 580 billion in the same period last year. Net revenue grew 28% year-on-year to nearly IDR 11 trillion in H1-2026, while total costs and expenses rose at a slower pace of only 17% YoY, demonstrating improving operational efficiency. This marks GOTO's second consecutive profitable reporting period, a significant milestone for one of Indonesia's largest publicly listed tech companies.

medium.title: Tomato Prices Collapse, Government Calls on Regional Administrations to Launch 'Buy Local' Campaign
medium.summary: The National Food Agency (Bapanas) has launched a 'buy local' initiative to support tomato farmers in Cianjur, West Java, after farm-gate prices plummeted from around Rp 12,000/kg to as low as Rp 1,000–1,600/kg due to oversupply. Bapanas is facilitating purchases at Rp 6,500/kg and urging regional governments to mobilize relevant agencies to absorb the harvest. This highlights ongoing food price volatility and the government's reactive approach to agricultural market management.

medium.title: Prabowo: Village Cooperatives (Kopdes Merah Putih) Will Eliminate Loan Sharks, Saving Hundreds of Trillions
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto stated that the Merah Putih Village Cooperative (Kopdes) program is designed to eliminate predatory lending practices by providing affordable financial services to rural farmers, who currently face loan sharks charging up to 1% interest per day. The initiative aims to significantly reduce the cost of agricultural financing and boost rural productivity. This represents a major rural financial inclusion push with potential large-scale impact on agricultural sector financing and rural economic conditions.

medium.title: Village Cooperative Managers' Salaries to Be Funded by State Budget for Two Years
medium.summary: Cooperative Minister Ferry Juliantono confirmed that managers of the Merah Putih Village/Urban Cooperatives (KDKMP) will have their salaries funded through the state budget (APBN) for an initial two-year period, after which individual cooperatives are expected to become self-sustaining. The arrangement will be formalized through a Presidential Regulation (Perpres) on cooperative governance. This has implications for state budget expenditure and the long-term financial viability of the nationwide cooperative program.

medium.title: Social Assistance to Be Distributed Through Red-White Village Cooperatives, Pilot Program in August
medium.summary: The government plans to channel social assistance (bansos) through the newly established Red-White Village Cooperatives (Kopdes Merah Putih/KDKMP), with a pilot program set to launch at the end of August 2026. The pilot will initially cover 900 cooperatives that are ready to operate, according to the Minister of Social Affairs Saifullah Yusuf. This initiative represents a significant shift in social assistance distribution infrastructure and could impact financial inclusion and rural economic activity across Indonesia.

medium.title: Antam Gold Price Falls Again Today, Down Rp 12,000 to Rp 2,601,000 per Gram
medium.summary: Antam 24-karat gold prices continued their downward trend on Wednesday, dropping another Rp 12,000 per gram to Rp 2,601,000, the lowest level in the past month. The buyback price also fell Rp 15,000 to Rp 2,346,000 per gram. Investors holding gold as a safe-haven asset should note the ongoing correction after prices peaked at Rp 2,670,000 within the last month.

medium.title: Malaysia One Step Away from Becoming a Developed Nation, Records 5.8% GDP Growth in Q2 2026
medium.summary: Malaysia's government announced the country is only 7.1% away from crossing the World Bank's high-income nation threshold, supported by 5.8% GDP growth in Q2 2026, inflation held at 1.9%, and unemployment at 3%. Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah emphasized that surpassing the threshold is not the end goal, but rather ensuring growth translates to better wages and quality jobs. This development is relevant for Indonesian investors and policymakers as a regional benchmark and potential indicator of competitive pressure for foreign investment flows in Southeast Asia.

medium.title: Prabowo: All Experts Predict Indonesia Will Become the World's 4th Largest Economy in 25 Years, Surpassing France and Germany
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto cited global expert forecasts projecting Indonesia will become the world's fourth-largest economy within 25 years, surpassing France, Germany, and the UK. The remarks were made during the inauguration of IPDN civil service graduates, framing their generation as future leaders who will realize this economic ambition. While aspirational in nature, the statement reflects the administration's long-term economic growth narrative relevant for assessing Indonesia's investment climate outlook.

medium.title: National Internship Allowances to Rise Next Year, Aligned with Minimum Wage Increases
medium.summary: Minister of Manpower Yassierli announced that stipends for the National Internship Program will increase next year in line with regional minimum wage (UMP/UMK) adjustments, with current allowances reaching up to Rp 5.9 million per month in areas like Bekasi and Karawang. The government has expanded the program quota from 100,000 participants in 2025 to 150,000 in 2026, with approximately 30% of last year's participants receiving job offers from their host companies. This signals growing government investment in workforce development and has implications for labor market dynamics and business hiring costs.

medium.title: UK Supports Indonesia's CPTPP Accession as Economic Partnership Is Strengthened
medium.summary: Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto met with UK Trade Commissioner for Asia Pacific Martin Kent to strengthen the Indonesia-UK Economic Growth Partnership (EGP) signed in January 2026, with the UK expressing support for Indonesia's accession to the CPTPP trade bloc. Key cooperation priorities include human resource development, energy, investment, and sustainable economic transition. CPTPP membership would significantly expand Indonesia's trade access and investment appeal to a broader set of global markets.

medium.title: PELNI Builds 3 New Ships Worth Rp 4.5 Trillion, Design Contracted to Italian Firm
medium.summary: State-owned shipping company PELNI is procuring three new passenger vessels worth Rp 4.5 trillion, funded through Rp 4 trillion in state capital injection (PMN) and Rp 500 billion in internal funds, with an Italian firm winning the ship design tender. Each vessel will have a capacity of approximately 1,000 passengers, and the design phase alone is expected to take around 17 months. This large capital expenditure reflects continued government investment in national maritime infrastructure and has relevance for related industries and suppliers.

medium.title: President Prabowo: Global Experts Predict Indonesia Will Become World's 4th Largest Economy in 25 Years
medium.summary: President Prabowo cited widespread forecasts from global experts that Indonesia will surpass France, Germany, and the UK to become the world's fourth-largest economy within 25 years. The statement was made during the inauguration of IPDN graduates, positioning them as future leaders who will drive this economic transformation. While forward-looking and aspirational, this narrative reinforces the government's long-term growth agenda and may support investor sentiment toward Indonesia's economic trajectory.

medium.title: Malaysia One Step Away from High-Income Nation Status, Economy Grows 5.8% in Q2 2026
medium.summary: Malaysia's government announced its GNI per capita is now only 7.1% below the World Bank's high-income threshold, supported by 5.8% GDP growth in Q2 2026, inflation at 1.9%, and unemployment at 3%. This development is relevant to Indonesian investors and policymakers as it highlights the competitive regional economic landscape in Southeast Asia. Malaysia's trajectory may increase pressure on Indonesia to accelerate its own structural reforms to remain competitive for foreign investment.

medium.title: Cooperatives Minister: Gen Z Interest in Cooperatives Continues to Rise
medium.summary: Minister of Cooperatives Ferry Juliantono highlighted growing interest among Gen Z and millennials in cooperative-based economic models, citing new registrations of content creator, millennial farmer, and animator cooperatives. The minister emphasized improved financial literacy among young Indonesians and the government's commitment to supporting youth-led cooperatives. This trend reflects a broader push to align Indonesia's cooperative sector with the digital economy and could open new SME and fintech-related investment themes.

medium.title: OJK Targets IDR 250 Trillion in IPO Fundraising This Year; IDR 125.7 Trillion Already Collected
medium.summary: Indonesia's Financial Services Authority (OJK) is targeting IDR 250 trillion in capital market fundraising through public offerings in 2026, with IDR 125.73 trillion already raised as of June 30, 2026 — exactly halfway to the target at the midpoint of the year. Despite ongoing global market challenges, OJK maintains a positive outlook for the remainder of 2026, citing sustained corporate interest in using capital markets as a funding source. Investors should monitor whether fundraising momentum can be maintained in the second half amid global headwinds.

medium.title: Indonesia Stock Exchange Needs 30 IPOs Per Year to Reach Target of 1,100 Listed Companies
medium.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) has set an ambitious target of 1,100 listed companies with a market capitalization of IDR 30,000 trillion by 2030, requiring approximately 30 new IPOs per year from the current base of 963 listed companies. However, only seven new companies have completed IPOs so far in 2026, highlighting a significant gap between the current pace and the required rate. This underscores structural challenges in deepening Indonesia's capital market and may prompt regulatory incentives to attract more companies to list.

medium.title: National Internship Stipend to Rise Next Year in Line with Minimum Wage Increases
medium.summary: Indonesia's Minister of Manpower, Yassierli, announced that stipends for the National Internship Program will increase next year in line with provincial and regional minimum wage adjustments. Currently, participants receive full government-funded stipends of around IDR 5.7 million per month in Jakarta and IDR 5.9 million in Bekasi and Karawang, with the 2026 quota expanded to 150,000 participants from 100,000 in 2025. Approximately 30% of last year's participants received direct job offers from their host companies, signaling the program's growing role in addressing youth unemployment.
